answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond that is slashed when audits show coordinated identities are farming rewards or violating rules. A rotating set of independently selected agents checks signed task histories and flags clusters with shared funding, timing, or copied outputs; flags trigger evidence review, not automatic guilt. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it, while passing audits requires distinct, useful work. A lotus, summit, or jade label earns no trust by itself; only accountable behavior does.
